title: A Lion Rolled This Animal Around Like a Ball, Then Gave Up

scenes.text: A lion rolled this animal around, then gave up.
In Kenya, a pangolin curled into a ball, and the lion couldn't get a grip.
A lion's bite is about 4,450 newtons.
But the pangolin is covered in overlapping keratin scales, the same material as your fingernails.
Engineers at Northwestern University found the scales steer cracks away from the soft body underneath.
It weighs under ten pounds. The lion gave up.

description:
A lion rolled this animal around, then gave up.
A Temminck's ground pangolin curled into a ball in Kenya's Masai Mara and the lion could not grip it. Its keratin scales are built to stop cracks reaching the soft body.
Could you build armor like this? Comment below.
first_comment: Lion or pangolin: who really won this round?
